q-110404.name: Question 1
q-110404.problem:
Given the joint probability distribution for two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ below, find $\text{E}[5X-2Y].$

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.25$ | $0.15$ | $0.2$ |
q-110404.worked_solution:
Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. | $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | ${f}_{X}$ | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | $X=0$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ | $0.4$ | | $X=1$ | $0.25$ | $0.15$ | $0.2$ | $0.6$ | | ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.3$ | $0.25$ | $0.45$ | $1$ | Therefore, the probability mass functions for $X$ and $Y$ are given by the following tables:
$x$ $0$ $1$
${f}_{X}(x)$ $0.4$ $0.6$

$y$ $0$ $1$ $2$
${f}_{Y}(y)$ $0.3$ $0.25$ $0.45$

Now, we can compute the expected values for $X$ and $Y:$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\,{f}_{X}({x}_{i}) \\ & =0\cdot 0.4+1\cdot 0.6 \\ & =0+0.6 \\ & =0.6\end{aligned} $$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}\,{f}_{Y}({y}_{i}) \\ & =0\cdot 0.3+1\cdot 0.25+2\cdot 0.45 \\ & =0+0.25+0.9 \\ & =1.15.\end{aligned} $$ Finally, using the properties of expectation, we obtain $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[5X-2Y] & =5\,\text{E}[X]-2\,\text{E}[Y] \\ & =5(0.6)-2(1.15) \\ & =3-2.3 \\ & =0.7.\end{aligned} $$

f Y=0 Y=1 Y=2 fX
X=0 0.05 0.1 0.25 0.4
X=1 0.25 0.15 0.2 0.6
fY 0.3 0.25 0.45 1

Therefore, the probability mass functions for X and Y are given by the following tables:

x 0 1
fX(x) 0.4 0.6

y 0 1 2
fY(y) 0.3 0.25 0.45

E[Y]=∑i=1nyifY(yi)=0⋅0.3+1⋅0.25+2⋅0.45=0+0.25+0.9=1.15.

q-143564.name: Question 2
q-143564.problem:
Given the joint probability distribution for two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ below, find $\text{E}[X].$

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=-1$ | $0.05$ | $0.05$ | $0.2$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.15$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ |
q-143564.worked_solution:
Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals.

| $f(x,y)$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=-1$ | $0.05$ | $0.05$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.15$ | $0.4$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.15$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $…$ | $…$ | $…$ | $1$ |

Therefore, the probability mass function for  $X$ is given by the following table:

| $x$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{X}(x)$ | $0.3$ | $0.4$ | $0.3$ |

Finally, the  expected value of $X$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\,{f}_{X}({x}_{i}) \\  & =(-1)\cdot 0.3+1\cdot 0.4+3\cdot 0.3 \\  & =-0.3+0.4+0.9 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-143571.problem:
Given the joint probability distribution for two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ below, find $\text{E}[2X-3Y].$

| $f$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.25$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.2$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.15$ | $0.15$ |

${f}_{X}(x)$ $0.35$ $0.35$ $0.3$

$y$ $2$ $3$
${f}_{Y}(y)$ $0.6$ $0.4$

Now, we can compute the expected values for $X$ and $Y:$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\,{f}_{X}({x}_{i}) \\ & =1\cdot 0.35+2\cdot 0.35+4\cdot 0.3 \\ & =0.35+0.7+1.2 \\ & =2.25\end{aligned} $$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}\,{f}_{Y}({y}_{i}) \\ & =2\cdot 0.6+3\cdot 0.4 \\ & =1.2+1.2 \\ & =2.4.\end{aligned} $$ Finally, using the properties of expectation, we obtain $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[2X-3Y] & =2\,\text{E}[X]-3\,\text{E}[Y] \\ & =2(2.25)-3(2.4) \\ & =4.5-7.2 \\ & =-2.7.\end{aligned} $$

q-149614.name: Question 6
q-149614.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}(x+2y), & 1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{17}{30},$ find $\text{E}[X+2Y].$
q-149614.worked_solution:
We're given $\text{E}[Y].$ So, we first need to compute $\text{E}[X].$

The marginal density function for $X$ when $1\le x\le 2$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{2}{5}(x+2y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{5}{[xy+{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}(x+1-0) \\  & =\frac{2(x+1)}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the  expected value of $X$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}x\cdot \frac{2(x+1)}{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{5}{\int }_{1}^{2}({x}^{2}+x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{5}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}(\frac{8}{3}+2-\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{23}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X+2Y] & =\text{E}[X]+2\text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{23}{15}+2(\frac{17}{30}) \\  & =\frac{23}{15}+\frac{17}{15} \\  & =\frac{40}{15} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-149609.name: Question 7
q-149609.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{7}(x+\sqrt{y}), & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{4}{7},$ find $\text{E}[2X+Y].$
q-149609.worked_solution:
We're given $\text{E}[X].$ So, we first need to compute $\text{E}[Y].$

The marginal density function for $Y$ when $0\le y\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{6}{7}(x+\sqrt{y})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{6}{7}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+x\sqrt{y}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{6}{7}(\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{y}) \\  & =\frac{3}{7}(2\sqrt{y}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the  expected value of $Y$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot \frac{3}{7}(2\sqrt{y}+1)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{7}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2{y}^{3/2}+y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{7}{[\frac{4}{5}{y}^{5/2}+\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{7}(\frac{4}{5}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{39}{70}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2X+Y] & =2\,\text{E}[X]+\text{E}[Y] \\  & =2(\frac{4}{7})+(\frac{39}{70}) \\  & =\frac{80+39}{70} \\  & =\frac{17}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot \frac{2(3+y)}{7}.\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{7}{\int }_{0}^{1}3y+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{7}{[\frac{3{y}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{2}{7}(\frac{3}{2}+\frac{1}{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{2}{7}\cdot \frac{11}{6} \\  & =\frac{11}{21}.\end{aligned}

$$
